You plan to visit 8 European cities for 20 days in total. You only take direct flights to commute between cities. You want to spend 2 days in Oslo. From day 16 to day 17, there is a annual show you want to attend in Oslo. You plan to stay in Reykjavik for 5 days. You want to meet a friend in Reykjavik between day 9 and day 13. You would like to visit Stockholm for 4 days. You want to spend 4 days in Munich. You plan to visit relatives in Munich between day 13 and day 16. You plan to stay in Frankfurt for 4 days. You have to attend a workshop in Frankfurt between day 17 and day 20. You would like to visit Barcelona for 3 days. You would like to visit Bucharest for 2 days. You want to spend 3 days in Split.

Here are the cities that have direct flights:
Reykjavik and Munich, Munich and Frankfurt, Split and Oslo, Reykjavik and Oslo, Bucharest and Munich, Oslo and Frankfurt, Bucharest and Barcelona, Barcelona and Frankfurt, Reykjavik and Frankfurt, Barcelona and Stockholm, Barcelona and Reykjavik, Stockholm and Reykjavik, Barcelona and Split, Bucharest and Oslo, Bucharest and Frankfurt, Split and Stockholm, Barcelona and Oslo, Stockholm and Munich, Stockholm and Oslo, Split and Frankfurt, Barcelona and Munich, Stockholm and Frankfurt, Munich and Oslo, Split and Munich.

Find a trip plan of visiting the cities for 20 days by taking direct flights to commute between them.

Please output the trip plan in the following JSON format:
{"itinerary": [{"day_range": "Day X-Y", "place": "<CITY>"}]}. Include all city visits with their day ranges. Do not include separate flight entries in the JSON output.

IMPORTANT: When you fly from city A to city B on day X, that day counts for BOTH cities. For example:
- If you stay in Venice from Day 1-3 and fly to Vienna on Day 3, then:
  - Venice: Day 1-3 (3 days)
  - Vienna: Day 3-6 (4 days, including the flight day)
- The flight day (Day 3) is counted for both Venice and Vienna.
- Do NOT create separate flight entries in the JSON.

Below is one complete 20‐day itinerary that meets all your requirements. In this plan you spend a total of 27 “raw” city‐days but each flight “day” counts for both the city you’re leaving and the city you’re entering – so 7 overlaps subtract to give 20 travel days. (In the plan below the four “fixed–event” cities are forced into the following calendar slots: you’re in Reykjavík for 5 days spanning Day 8–12 (so you can meet your friend between Day 9 and Day 12), then in Munich for 4 days from Day 12–15 (so that on Days 13–15 you are there with relatives), then in Oslo for 2 days from Day 16–17 (perfect for the annual show held from Day 16–17), and finally in Frankfurt for 4 days from Day 17–20 (covering the workshop from Day 17–20). To “link” these fixed‐time visits you take advantage of direct flights that also let you intersperse three “flexible” visits in the very first part of your trip. (Remember that when you fly on the last day of one stay you immediately begin your next stay.) 

In the itinerary below the three flexible “pre‐fixed” segments come first. They visit Stockholm for 4 days (Day 1–4), then Split for 3 days (Day 4–6) and then Barcelona for 3 days (Day 6–8). (Barcelona was chosen as last in the flexible block because – among your four “extra” cities – it is the only one that offers a direct flight to Reykjavík.) In order to include Bucharest (which does not “chain” well with Stockholm or Split) it is moved into the fixed block between Munich and Oslo (since Munich and Oslo both fly directly to or from Bucharest). With this “insertion” the fixed‐event block has 5 cities (Reykjavik, Munich, Bucharest, Oslo, Frankfurt) and automatically spans the 13 net days from Day 8 to Day 20. (Although Munich is “entered” on Day 12, you are then in Munich on Days 13–15 – i.e. in time to visit relatives “between Day 13 and Day 16”.)

The detailed day‐by‐day plan is as follows:

• Day 1–4: Stockholm (4 days)  
  Fly on Day 4 to…  
• Day 4–6: Split (3 days)  
  Fly on Day 6 to…  
• Day 6–8: Barcelona (3 days)  
  Fly on Day 8 to…  
• Day 8–12: Reykjavík (5 days; meets friend during Day 9–12)  
  Fly on Day 12 to…  
• Day 12–15: Munich (4 days; relatives visit occurs during Day 13–15)  
  Fly on Day 15 to…  
• Day 15–16: Bucharest (2 days)  
  Fly on Day 16 to…  
• Day 16–17: Oslo (2 days; annual show from Day 16–17)  
  Fly on Day 17 to…  
• Day 17–20: Frankfurt (4 days; workshop held from Day 17–20)

All flights used are direct (for example, Stockholm→Split [direct], Split→Barcelona [direct], Barcelona→Reykjavik [direct], Reykjavík→Munich, Munich→Bucharest, Bucharest→Oslo, and Oslo→Frankfurt).

Below is the JSON output in the requested format:

{
  "itinerary": [
    {"day_range": "Day 1-4", "place": "Stockholm"},
    {"day_range": "Day 4-6", "place": "Split"},
    {"day_range": "Day 6-8", "place": "Barcelona"},
    {"day_range": "Day 8-12", "place": "Reykjavik"},
    {"day_range": "Day 12-15", "place": "Munich"},
    {"day_range": "Day 15-16", "place": "Bucharest"},
    {"day_range": "Day 16-17", "place": "Oslo"},
    {"day_range": "Day 17-20", "place": "Frankfurt"}
  ]
}

In this solution the scheduled day ranges meet these specific requirements:
 – You begin your trip in Stockholm (4 days), then visit Split (3 days) and Barcelona (3 days).  
 – On Day 8 you fly (counted in both stays) into Reykjavík and spend 5 days there (Day 8–12) so you can meet your friend between Day 9–12.  
 – You then fly from Reykjavík (Day 12) to Munich (entering on Day 12 and spending Days 13–15 there so that most of your Munich stay falls between Day 13 and 16).  
 – Next you fly on Day 15 to Bucharest for 2 days (Day 15–16), then on Day 16 you fly to Oslo so you are there on Day 16–17 for the annual show,  
 – and finally you fly on Day 17 to Frankfurt for your 4‐day workshop (Day 17–20).

This itinerary uses only the listed direct flight routes and overall satisfies your trip‐planning conditions.
